title: A Snake Longer Than a School Bus Once Lived in India

scenes.text: A snake longer than a school bus once slithered through India.
Scientists named it Vasuki, after the mythical serpent around the neck of the god Shiva. It lived 47 million years ago.
Researchers pulled 27 giant backbones out of a coal mine in Gujarat. Some are over 11 centimeters wide.
That puts the snake at 11 to 15 meters long, rivaling Titanoboa, the biggest snake ever known.
It was far too heavy to move fast, so it likely hunted like an anaconda: waiting in ambush, then squeezing.
Back then the region was a steamy tropical swamp, and warmth helps giant cold-blooded reptiles grow.
Today it's a dusty mine. Would you have survived India 47 million years ago?

description:
A snake longer than a school bus once slithered through India.
Vasuki indicus, described by palaeontologists at IIT Roorkee from 27 vertebrae found in a lignite mine in Kutch, Gujarat, lived about 47 million years ago and is estimated at 11 to 15 metres long, rivalling Titanoboa.
Would you have survived in the India of 47 million years ago?
